about: The one table behind Speed up (quantization/speed_up.py reads it): one row per engine. The core is engine-neutral; a row names the module in quantization/head_writers/ that holds that engine's parts, and the names of its functions: stock (is this engine stock), plan (the output layer and whether the target is lighter), write (the copy), accuracy (original against copy), and optionally speed (decode rows at given contexts and batches) with device (target id, name, backend, memory_bytes and budget_bytes the engine may use of the GPU in this machine; speed results are a list in the copy's record, one entry per GPU); a row without speed is kept on accuracy alone. formats are checkpoint formats (head_writers.detect), never model names. runs says whether the engine is built; why says why not. Adding an engine is a row and a writer module, no core edit. parts maps each part (the parts table below) the engine writes to its plan function and what its writer needs (file: the new weights' file, whose presence also marks a source that already has the part light; targets; prefix: where the part's modules sit in this engine's checkpoints); mtp names the function that measures speed with MTP on (mtp_ks: the one that says the draft counts it starts from), returning per depth the context, each prompt's tok/s without drafts (base) and at each k (ks), and each prompt's output hash (tokens). One part per run: a part added to a copy is a copy of that copy, gated against it, with the links into it hashed in the record.

parts.label: output layer
parts.about: lm_head: read on every token, so it changes the main model's answers: the next-token agreement gate, then plain decode speed. untied: refused when config.json ties it to the embedding

parts.label: MTP draft layer
parts.note: not checked: only the MTP draft layer changed and every drafted token is checked by the main model; outputs can still differ at floating-point near-ties, as they do with MTP itself (the record counts the prompts whose tokens match between the arms)
parts.about: the draft layer's Linear modules the checkpoint keeps unquantized (the engine row's prefix and the checkpoint's ignore list). Every drafted token is checked by the main model, so outputs differ only at floating-point near-ties, as with MTP itself and with any recompiled graph (2026-11-12: k=3 against k=0 on one copy matched 1 of 8 short prompts; a byte-identical main model in a new compiled graph matched 2 of 8 short and 7 of 8 long): no agreement gate, the matching prompts recorded, not gated (note). The gate is speed with MTP on, run source, copy, source again on the same prompts (at least the count data/mtp_prompts.json's size derives, at the short depth; a long depth with fewer documents is judged and said underpowered) and the same long-depth real text (data/mtp_long_corpus.json; the arms' input ids are compared by hash), each without drafts and at each draft count k: the source and the copy each run the derived sweep (core/draft_count.sweep_next: from collectors/mtp.KS, one k more while a larger one could still win), and the source runs again at every k either sweep reached. Per prompt, the copy at its best k over the source at its best k (the source's two runs averaged where both ran that k, else its second run; each arm's best k by median tok/s, chosen again inside every bootstrap resample of the prompts, seed 0); kept only if the lower end of the 95% interval of the median is above 1 plus the source's own change between its two runs (at the source's best k, or the largest change over the ks both its runs share when its first sweep stopped short of that k), at every depth. Recorded beside it: the factor with MTP over without (each arm over its own run without drafts; each arm compiles its own graph) and the factor without drafts (copy over source), whose product is the headline. The baseline is the source: the original, or the copy this part is added to (a second command: derive one part per run)

threshold.about: the copy's pooled next-token agreement with the original over the documents of data/gate_corpus.json (8 Project Gutenberg excerpts of natural prose the original did not write, hashed here; a different hash refuses; set by the owner 2026-11-10 after the review found the original's own continuation too easy a text), judged by quantization/speed_up.bar, the one place the rule is computed (Speed up's copies and tune's output-changing knobs). Derived, owner-approved 2026-11-13; it replaces the fixed 95 (2026-11-10), its 5-point budget and the 0.90 hard minimum (2026-11-13 morning). Stage 1: d = 1 - agreement; pass iff d_copy - d_floor <= t SE (t: Student t at confidence, k - 1 df for k documents; SE the document bootstrap SD of the difference, paired by document and position, one estimate) and every document's copy_i - floor_i is within Sidak's z for k documents times sqrt(var_c,i + var_f,i); an engine with no floor goes straight to needs_eval. Stage 1 not passed: needs_eval, decided only by a paired downstream eval against the engine's own eval noise (eval, speed_up.noninferior). Reviewed 2026-11-13: the bootstrap alone over 8 documents measures how damage is spread, not its size. The interval is clustered by document. Fewer scored positions than min_positions and the gate refuses to decide

noise.about: The engine's own noise floor d_floor (2026-11-13): the original checked against itself, on the same corpus and setup, under the change its engine declares must not matter (engines, read by Speed up and tune through speed_up.perturbation; quantization/speed_up.noise_floor). Cost: one more accuracy check, once per key (2026-11-13, Flash-Next IQ1_M on llama.cpp v1.0.0: 227 s beside the copy's own 222 s; boltbeam-runs/gate-floor-20261113). Cached in ~/.boltbeam/noise_floor (speed_up.FLOORS) under a hash of the model's files (path, size, mtime; every shard of a split), the engine build, the texts, the check's arguments with the change, and the engine's accuracy module: any of them different is a new key and measures again; delete the folder to force it. The excess d_copy - d_floor understates damage when the copy's flips land on the floor's own near-ties, so it is a lower bound. Why: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ1_M, llama.cpp 7592b61d3, RTX 5090 (boltbeam-runs/llama-dense-20261113 gate/): stock against stock at the same batch shape 100.00 (bit-deterministic), at another batch shape 95.42 (worst document 88.2, mean KL 0.0152) with no code change; a kernel change 95.70, q8_0 KV 95.87: the fixed 95 nearly failed the engine against itself. An engine not in engines has no floor: every copy that changes any answer waits on a task eval, and its eval noise is the original run again. vLLM is not in engines: its accuracy function takes no engine arguments, so no principled no-op change (another max_num_batched_tokens chunking would be one) can be passed to it yet. The cache key also holds the engine build and device (the writer's build and device), and the gate's own agreement code; an entry whose stored key differs, or that is not whole, is measured again.

llama.cpp.says: batches of 4 tokens in place of 512
llama.cpp.about: the noise floor's change that must not matter (threshold.noise): the original against itself at a batch of 4 tokens (-b 4 -ub 4: the MTP verify shape) where the check otherwise reads 512 at a time. Different matmul kernels and reduction orders, the same weights. Measured 2026-11-13 on Flash-Next IQ1_M (gate/o-sbig*.txt, the same pair the other way round): 95.42 pooled. vLLM declares none yet (not measured), so it has no floor

eval.unchanged: unchanged (this engine declares no change that must not matter, so its eval noise is the original run again)
eval.command: run your eval three times on the same items, each row in the row format (id, correct: true or false, finish: stop or length, model: the checkpoint's path, config: the eval's settings, one value for every row): {source} into {original_rows}, {copy} into {copy_rows}, and {source} again {again} into {noise_rows} (the engine's own eval noise, cached per model, engine build and items); then `boltbeam derive lighter-head {copy} --verify` judges them
eval.about: Stage 2, for a copy that needs_eval (speed_up.noninferior, judged by verify): D, the copy's paired net loss against the engine's own noise run on the same items (the original run again under the engine's declared change, or unchanged when it declares none); the standard non-inferiority rule at threshold.confidence against a tolerance fixed before the copy's data: fail when D - z SE > tolerance, pass when D + z SE <= tolerance, else inconclusive with how many more items an equal copy would need at power. tolerance, decided by the owner 2026-11-14: psi0, the engine's own gross eval churn (the share of answers its noise run changes against the original), measured per model, engine build, original rows and eval settings: relative to the engine's own noise, measured, not picked; said in the words every time. An engine whose noise run changes no answer has no psi0 and is refused (declare a perturbation). Also expressible, not the default: 0 (pass only when shown no worse than the noise run; the second review's rule) or a fixed share. max_truncation: an arm with more than 5% of its answers cut at the length limit (finish=length) is inconclusive, BoltBeam's eval budget rule (owner 2026-11-11, eval budgets are derived: a pilot over 5% truncation blocks the launch). Rerunning for "N more items" re-rolls all three arms, so repeating the eval until it passes inflates the error rate: run the noise arm once and add the new items to all three arms together. BoltBeam ships no eval harness: any eval that writes these rows will do.

expect.about: Seconds each stage is expected to take: floor + per_gib x the checkpoint's GiB. NOT MEASURED: set by hand 2026-11-10 from the order of magnitude of the first runs, so a screen shows them as an estimate (about) until a run's own step times replace them.

mtp.about: The MTP part's speed_measure, derived from what quantization/speed_up.measure_mtp runs (mtp_seconds): engine starts (each run's k=0 and one per k, from the row's mtp_ks to core/draft_count.K_MAX) x per_start (the long depth is the shipped real text, data/mtp_long_corpus.json, nothing generated first since 2026-11-12: the term for the source's own continuation, 5.4 s per GiB per 1k tokens, is gone). MEASURED on one run only (one point: 27B, RTX 5090, vLLM 0.31), 2026-11-12, a 27B compressed-tensors copy of 16.45 GiB (storage/boltbeam-runs/derive-mtp-27b-20261112, log times in the copy's speed_up_mtp): 134 to 150 s per start in the source and copy runs, median 139; the source's first k=0 took 854 s, 715 s more than a start. That run swept the source and the copy to the K_MAX cap, so it sits at the TOP of the range: its measurement took 5,093 s (84.9 min; source 2,235, copy 1,600, source again 1,258 at 114 s a start) against 5,302 s (88.4 min) estimated; the job (write and the three runs) 85.2 min, 5,109 s, each run sweeping k=1..10 (all hit the then K_MAX cap of 10 at the long depth; that depth was the model's own looping continuation, so those sweeps followed repetition, not text; the top of the range, k=16, is extrapolated by the formula, unmeasured). The low end (each sweep stopping at its first ks) has never been measured, so it is likely optimistic. The split of per_start into floor and per GiB is set by hand (one size measured). per_prompt and per_document: the decode seconds one short prompt (data/mtp_prompts.json) and one long-depth document (data/mtp_long_corpus.json) add to a start, MEASURED on the same three runs (mean over k=1..10: 1.63 and 3.75 s, docs/evidence/mtp-prompt-count-20261112/derivation.json measured_seconds); the floor was 60 at that run's 8 prompts and 8 long prompts and is 60 less 8 x (1.63 + 3.75), so that run's starts still give 139 s

the MTP draft head is a sidecar GGUF (llama-server -md, --spec-type draft-mtp), measured with the main model it drafts for (--main) by the module data/engine_knobs.json names (engines.llama.cpp.mtp, through collectors/mtp.measure); the copy is a new sidecar beside it, the main GGUF untouched

recipe.found: by hand, 2026-11-11 (2 variants tried, not searched)
recipe.evidence: boltbeam-runs/tunedhead-20261111.md, head A: from the unsloth Q8_0 head of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (llama.cpp 7592b61d3, llama-quantize --allow-requantize), 1,850,222,720 B, sha256 34de268042c84a92c05cc4f41208819161d2446f20e55e762ce6e06f89a1c7d6 (the notes' c1d6 ending is a typo); on an RTX 5090, all in VRAM, draft-mtp k=3, 4 long prompts x 3 reps x 2 runs: acceptance 0.570 (0.587 over all 8 prompts; the Q8_0 head 0.627, the Q2_K-small head 0.478), 182.5 tok/s median against 129.0 without MTP. The notes say experts down Q2_K: its 640 columns do not divide into Q2_K blocks of 256 and llama-quantize wrote Q4_0 (tuned-quant-A.log, the file's header), so the recipe says Q4_0. Which tensors carry the acceptance is not isolated (confounds-20261111.md (b))
